title: Electric field magnitude
description: Essential: Correctly calculates E = U_ac / (2L) = 1500 N/C.

title: Potential at point C
description: Essential: Correctly calculates φ_C = -30 V using the given zero potential at B and the field.

title: Work A to C
description: Essential: Correctly calculates W_AC = q * U_AC = -6.0 × 10⁻⁹ J for the given charge.

title: Total work B-C-D-P
description: Essential: Correctly states the total work is 0 J, as the path starts and ends on the same equipotential surface (B and P).

title: Uses potential difference correctly
description: Important: Applies the formula for uniform field E = ΔV/Δd, correctly identifying Δd_ac = 2L.

title: Applies work-energy principle
description: Important: Uses W = qΔV for work done by the electric field, with correct sign for the charge.

title: Recognizes equipotential surfaces
description: Important: Identifies that B, C, D, and P lie on equipotential surfaces and understands work along/back to an equipotential is zero.

title: Sign error in work
description: Pitfall: Uses W = |q||ΔV| or misapplies the sign of the charge relative to the potential difference.

title: Distance misinterpretation
description: Pitfall: Uses d_ac = L instead of 2L when calculating the electric field strength.

title: Path dependence misconception
description: Pitfall: Attempts to sum work for each leg (B→C, C→D, D→P) individually, failing to recognize the conservative nature and equipotential endpoints.
